summary.text: A 38-year-old first-pregnancy woman at 35 weeks of gestation from a rural area in Rasht, Iran, with a history of pituitary microadenoma and hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, presented with gastrointestinal and respiratory problems; diarrhea, abdominal pain and severe dyspnea had been present since the fourth month of pregnancy. Eosinophils were 2% and the white blood cell count 9.2 × 10^(3)/μL.

Stool examination with agar plate culture, anti-S. stercoralis IgG ELISA (40.3 NTU) and molecular testing confirmed strongyloidiasis with S. stercoralis third-stage larvae. Treatment was deferred until after delivery; four weeks postpartum breastfeeding was discontinued for two weeks and ivermectin was given for two days, and post-partum treatment was effective. Breast milk tested one month after birth was negative.

article_limitations: Roster: the abstract names the newborn before the mother in the same sentence, so the newborn is p1 and the mother p2 by first mention; no number of individuals is stated literally, so reported_individual_count is null and both individuals are in the roster.
The newborn is identified only by the stool testing and the statement that it was born to the index mother; no age, sex, gestational age at birth or birth weight is given.
Discussion and introduction statements on strongyloidiasis, transmission and screening are general background and are not copied to patients.
Segment b00016 says treatment continued until after delivery, which conflicts with the deferral stated in b00001 and b00010; both statements are kept as source_conflict review_only facts.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; actual images inspected in the separate visual target.
